stem: Farm labourers who work during the sowing and harvesting seasons but remain without work for the rest of the year are said to face:
explanation: Seasonal unemployment occurs when work is available only in certain seasons, as in agriculture. Disguised unemployment is when more people work on a task than actually needed (each contributing little extra output).

section: Social Studies · Ch51 — Economics — Deep Practice
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Green Revolution in India, which significantly boosted foodgrain production from the 1960s onward, is closely associated with the work of:

options.option_text: Norman Borlaug alone, with no Indian scientist involved

explanation: M.S. Swaminathan led India's Green Revolution effort, adapting high-yield seed varieties. Verghese Kurien led the White Revolution (dairy/Operation Flood) instead; Homi Bhabha pioneered India's nuclear programme.

section: Social Studies · Ch51 — Economics — Deep Practice
subject: Social Studies
stem: 'Operation Flood', which made India the world's largest milk producer, is also known as India's:
explanation: Operation Flood (led by Verghese Kurien/Amul model) is the White Revolution in dairy. Green Revolution = foodgrains; Blue Revolution = fisheries; Yellow Revolution = oilseeds.

section: Social Studies · Ch51 — Economics — Deep Practice
subject: Social Studies
stem: The 'poverty line' in economic terms is generally defined based on a minimum level of:

options.option_text: Income or consumption expenditure needed to meet basic calorie/subsistence requirements
Educational qualification required for a job
Land ownership only, with no reference to income
Number of family members in a household

explanation: The poverty line is typically defined by a minimum income/expenditure level sufficient to meet basic subsistence needs (including a calorie norm) — not by education, land, or family size directly.
